_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for CAT retrospectives (retro/build_cat.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2013 were accepted before the open on their release days, except Q1 2008's and Q4 2010's (during the session). The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the guides for the current fiscal year (each field from the latest guide that states it, in either form) and the latest declared dividend (else the vintage's). Caterpillar's fiscal year is the calendar year; the recasts of the FY2006-FY2008 statements (8-K of 2009-05-14) and of the FY2008-FY2010 statements for the 2011 segments (8-K of 2011-05-23) are vintages of their own. EPS is profit per share - diluted, replaced by the company's figure where a filing publishes one excluding only one-offs (2001; 2009's $2.18 excluding redundancy costs); 2011 is $7.40 as reported, not the $7.79 excluding Bucyrus (a whole business, not a one-off), and 2012 is $8.48 as reported, with the Siwei impairment in it (no figure excluding it is published). From the 2011 segments a print reports Construction Industries, Resource Industries and Power Systems ('ci_m', 'ri_m', 'ps_m' in 'raw'), read as the successors of the Machinery and Engines lines ('lines_basis'). Per-share figures published before the 2-for-1 split of 2005-07-14 carry their publication dates ('eps_published', 'shares_published') so the split restates them. Guides: sales and revenues as a dollar level or range ('rev_guide_usd_b', read against the last full year) or as growth ('rev_guide_pct', on the last full year unless 'rev_growth_base_b' names another base); profit per share as a dollar level or range ('eps_guide'; the 2009 guides excluding redundancy costs, with the inclusive figure in 'eps_guide_note'; the 2011 guides including Bucyrus once it closed, with the figure excluding it in 'eps_guide_note'; 'near' and 'about' levels read as numbers) or as growth ('eps_growth', on the last full year unless 'eps_growth_base' names another base); words and one-sided bounds in 'rev_words' give no field. A print's growth and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw', $ millions; the builder re-derives and checks them), each against the year-ago quarter as the same release shows it. Rule T's raw figures are in 'rule_t'. From Q1 2014 Power Systems is Energy & Transportation ('et_m' in 'raw'); from the FY2013 vintage 'why_theme_tail' names the 10-K's carbon-emissions or climate-change wording, which the builder keeps in the 'why' with a clause that follows ENERGY_TRANSITION's status on AS_OF (live from 2015-12-12, scoped to reserves and refining). From 2013 the company's figure excluding restructuring costs (and, from the change to mark-to-market pension and OPEB accounting effective January 1, 2016, mark-to-market gains and losses; for 2016 also a goodwill impairment and a deferred tax valuation allowance) is the ACN-rule figure; the 8-K of 2016-05-16 recasting 2011-2015 for that change is a vintage of its own. A print may republish an earlier year's company figure ('restates', EPS only), which replaces it until a 10-K vintage published after the print. From 2018 the releases' sales-by-region tables give external, inter-segment and total sales by segment; the external column is read. Guides from 2018 are profit per share only (the company's adjusted range where both are given); a guide may withdraw named fields of its year ('withdrawn': the 8-K of 2020-03-26), which voids them in every earlier guide for that year. No later fact enters through this file.

rule_t._doc: Rule T over fiscal 1997-2006, the decade of the FY2006 10-K (the vintage public on 2008-01-04): each annual change from the latest 10-K published by then whose statement of results (sales and revenues, operating profit, profit per share - diluted) and enterprise-wide sales table (external sales of Machinery and Engines) report both years. Seams stay in, as published: the 1999-2002 10-Ks' Engines lines are external sales (intersegment engines excluded), the FY2005 and FY2006 10-Ks restate 2003-2005 (revenue reclassifications, SFAS 123R), the 2004 change is on the split basis and the earlier ones are not (growth rates do not depend on it), Progress Rail enters Machinery from June 2006, and 2001 operating profit and profit per share include the nonrecurring charges (the values are as published; only the EPS history uses the company's figure excluding them)

price_basis: Yahoo's CAT series is adjusted for the 2-for-1 splits of 1994-09-06, 1997-07-14 and 2005-07-14; no split follows 2005, so from 2008 Yahoo's close is the price as traded ($68.53 on 2008-01-04, $44.67 on 2008-12-31). Prices before 2005-07-14 are on the post-split basis in Yahoo's series, as are the per-share facts once the 'splits' record halves those published before that date.
